introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The lengths of rods from a certain factory are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ cm and standard deviation $6$ cm. It is known that $4.78\%$ of the rods have lengths greater than $82$ cm.

Find, to the nearest integer,
incertitudes: Question 8 (ii) : « the range, α (symmetrical about the mean) » est ambigu ; le corrigé calcule la demi-largeur α telle que P(μ - α < X < μ + α) = 0,75 (α ≈ 6,9, soit 7 cm à l'entier près, donc des longueurs entre 65 cm et 79 cm) et indique aussi l'amplitude totale de 14 cm.
Question 8 (iii) : avec z = 5/3 exact on obtient 0,4522 ; avec la table arrondie à z = 1,67 on trouve 0,4525. Le corrigé donne 0,4522 et signale l'écart de lecture de table.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the length of a rod, $X\sim N(\mu,\,6^2)$, and $Z = \dfrac{X-\mu}{6}\sim N(0,1)$. We are told $P(X>82) = 0.0478$, so
$$P\!\left(Z > \frac{82-\mu}{6}\right) = 0.0478 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Phi\!\left(\frac{82-\mu}{6}\right) = 1 - 0.0478 = 0.9522.$$

From the normal distribution tables, $\Phi(1.66) = 0.9515$ and $\Phi(1.67) = 0.9525$, so $0.9522$ corresponds to $z \approx 1.67$ (more precisely $1.6666$). Then
$$\frac{82-\mu}{6} = 1.67 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mu = 82 - 6(1.67) = 71.98.$$

$$\boxed{\,\mu \approx 72\ \text{cm}\,}$$

(With the unrounded $z = 1.6666\ldots = \tfrac53$ one gets exactly $\mu = 82 - 10 = 72.0$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: the range, $\alpha$ (symmetrical about the mean) within which $75\%$ of the lengths of the rods lie. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Now $X\sim N(72,\,6^2)$. We want $\alpha$ such that
$$P(72-\alpha < X < 72+\alpha) = 0.75.$$

In standard units, with $z_0 = \dfrac{\alpha}{6}$:
$$P(-z_0 < Z < z_0) = 0.75 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2\Phi(z_0) - 1 = 0.75 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Phi(z_0) = 0.875.$$

From the tables, $z_0 = 1.15$ (more precisely $1.1503$). Hence
$$\alpha = 6\times 1.15 = 6.9 \approx 7\ \text{cm}.$$

$$\boxed{\,\alpha \approx 7\ \text{cm}\ :\ 75\%\ \text{of the rods have lengths between } 65\ \text{cm and } 79\ \text{cm}\,}$$

(the range $72 \pm 6.9$ is $65.1 < X < 78.9$, i.e. $65$ to $79$ to the nearest integer, a total width of about $14$ cm).

questions.enonce_markdown: Find also, to 4 decimal places, the probability that a rod chosen at random has a length between $62$ cm and $72$ cm. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $X\sim N(72,\,6^2)$, standardise:
$$z_1 = \frac{62-72}{6} = -\frac53 \approx -1.667,\qquad z_2 = \frac{72-72}{6} = 0.$$

$$P(62<X<72) = P\!\left(-\tfrac53 < Z < 0\right) = \Phi(0) - \Phi\!\left(-\tfrac53\right) = \Phi\!\left(\tfrac53\right) - 0.5$$

since $\Phi(-z) = 1-\Phi(z)$. With $\Phi(1.6667) = 0.95221$:
$$P(62<X<72) = 0.95221 - 0.5 = 0.45221\ldots$$

$$\boxed{\,P(62<X<72) \approx 0.4522\,}$$

(Reading the tables with $z$ rounded to $1.67$ gives $\Phi(1.67) - 0.5 = 0.4525$; the calculator value for $z = \tfrac53$ is $0.4522$.)
